key_insight: Distinct optical emission signatures from laser reflection, near-infrared thermal emission, and visible emission can identify specific micro-welding defects and process-state transitions in real time.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical online defect assessment for laser micro-welding, helping operators detect application-critical faults such as lack of penetration, holes, and thickening before parts are accepted.
method: Simultaneously monitored three optical channels during high-speed laser micro-welding of thin stainless-steel sheets.
Intentionally varied welding power, focus, inter-sheet gap, and laser incidence angle to generate characteristic defects.
Trained a simple machine-learning classifier on chunked optical signals to label good weld, lack of weld, hole, and thickening.
evidence_signal: For off-axis welds, the classifier achieved recall above 90% for all but one class, and the optical signals showed distinct, reproducible signatures for each defect type.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on controlled defects and a limited exploratory case of spontaneous defects, so broader transferability and robustness in industrial settings still need validation.
paper_title: Characteristic defect detection in laser micro-welding using distinct optical signal signatures and machine learning
